headings: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
4.2 HardMatch: does VGGT encode its own failures?
The features know more than the outputs.
A negative result: routing to a matcher.
VGGT rarely fails on landmark photographs.
VGGT’s indoor failures are translation failures.
Transfer depends on the failure mode.

Right: ROC-AUC for predicting VGGT’s pose failures on held-out HardMatch categories, from VGGT’s own confidence and from the probe, on all pairs and on the half of the pairs VGGT is most confident about.

Bottom: second image with the epipolar lines implied by VGGT’s own predicted cameras (same colour as the point); for a correct pose each point lies on its line. “conf.”: percentile of VGGT’s point-map confidence among all pairs (higher = more confident); “probe”: out-of-fold failure probability. (d) VGGT is unconfident but correct, and the probe does not flag it. (e) A miss: extreme zoom on a confidently wrong pair.

Figure 3: Failure awareness emerges abruptly in the middle of the network, in both models. ROC-AUC for predicting VGGT’s pose failures on HardMatch from every block of (a) VGGT and (b) π3\pi^{3}, with a linear probe (blue) and with one training-free number, the cosine similarity between the two views’ pooled features (orange). Dashed: the model’s own confidence. Shaded: the per-image encoder. The probe is flat through the encoder and the first half of the cross-view layers, then rises within a few blocks; only in VGGT does the training-free similarity follow.
